correctness.rationale: For a fixed vacancy, jumping a boundary agent leaves just one occupied destination neighbor; an interior agent sees both vacancy neighbors. If end colors agree, Nash requires all opposite-color internal agents isolated; if ends differ, terminal runs are singleton and internal runs have lengths <=2 with an even number of runs. Counting opposite-color gaps gives C(r-1,b)+C(b-1,r); counting each alternating 2h+2-run arrangement gives 2 sum_h C(h,r-h-1)C(h,b-h-1). Summing generating functions over populations yields H_n=F_(n+2)+(-1,0,+1) indexed by n mod 3, with two monochromatic words included. The balanced central term is maximal in each run class and total distinct-end count grows phi^(2m+o(m)); division by C(2m,m) gives rate phi^2/4. Directly rebuilt exact rational relocation payoffs on all binary words n=3..12, checking entire formula composition by composition. Code does not substitute for all-n generating-function and asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 primary article proves potentiality/existence for one-vacancy regular graphs and bounds on efficiency, not full composition-resolved numbers. Crucially, the published 2026-11-02 Resultary theorem for balanced populations on odd cycles already proves the balanced run criterion, exact balanced census and welfare; these are PRIOR COVERED and receive no novelty credit. The present claim strictly extends to all positive unequal r,b, gives new same-end isolation cases and a Fibonacci total H_n with a periodic correction. Different variety-count and similarity-seeking objectives are not equivalent.

Known balanced rarity and welfare should be cited, not represented as first discovered.

value.rationale: A complete closed count of Nash configurations for every population split measures the full density of local optima, which a convergence/potential theorem does not supply. Its new unequal-end/equal-end split and periodic-corrected Fibonacci total cover all sizes, while the previously published balanced specialization supplies only one slice. The sharp exponential rarity is useful context but already substantially covered in a prior balanced theorem.

limitations: Strict Nash deviations only, one vacancy, two types, occupied-neighbor fractional diversity payoff.
